newsitem.title: GERMANY: German miners occupy town halls to protest at cuts.
newsitem.headline: German miners occupy town halls to protest at cuts.

text.p: Thousands of German coalminers on Monday occupied two town halls in the mining districts of the Ruhr valley and blocked the entrances to the headquarters of Bonn's ruling parties in protest at planned subsidy cuts.
Miners took control of the town halls in Luenen and Bergkamen in western Germany as tens of thousands set out for protests across the Ruhr district and the Saar state on the French border.

Germany's pit workers are enraged at government plans to reduce coal subsidies to 3.8 billion marks ($2.2 billion) from nine billion marks by the year 2005 -- plans they they say will force 10 pits to close and cost 50,000 jobs in already depressed areas.
The opposition Social Democrats (SPD) were due to decide at a leadership meeting in Berlin on Monday whether to boycott cooperation talks with the government on planned tax reforms.
The SPD rules both the key coal mining states of North Rhine-Westphalia and Saar, and it broke off the talks last week in protest at the planned subsidy cuts.

In Bonn, thousands of miners blocked the entrances to the headquarters of both the free-market Free Democrats (FDP), the driving force behind the subsidy cuts, and Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU).
The FDP was forced to move its regular Monday leadership meeting to parliament buildings nearby, while the CDU had already postponed its meeting earlier, for other reasons.

In the Ruhr valley town of Duisburg, around 2,000 miners from the Walsum colliery drove in convoy to the town labour office, and in Bottrop around 2,000 miners were setting off to protest outside the local CDU office.
In the Saar region, miners continued to block a motorway which is Germany's main route to Luxembourg. ($ = 1.707 German Marks)
